---
title: "The backbones and datasets"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
library(taxify)

# The tables are built from the manifest that ships with this build, so they
# match the installed package and need no network. list_backbones() and
# list_enrichments() read the session manifest cache; point it at that copy.
mp <- system.file("manifest_v3.json", package = "taxify")
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(mp, simplifyVector = FALSE)
assign("manifest", manifest, envir = taxify:::.taxify_env)

# A source_url is a full URL or a bare DOI; both become an absolute link.
href <- function(url) {
  ifelse(is.na(url) | grepl("^https?://", url), url,
         ifelse(grepl("^10\\.[0-9]", url), paste0("https://doi.org/", url),
                paste0("https://", url)))
}

# "Authors year" from the first citation of a manifest entry, linked to its
# DOI where it has one.
short_ref <- function(entry) {
  cit <- entry$citation
  if (is.null(cit) || length(cit) == 0L) return("")
  if (is.character(cit)) return(short_ref_text(cit[[1L]]))
  c1 <- if (!is.null(cit$authors)) cit else cit[[1L]]
  if (is.character(c1)) return(short_ref_text(c1))
  first <- sub(",.*$", "", c1$authors %||% "")
  n_auth <- length(strsplit(c1$authors %||% "", ",\\s*")[[1L]])
  who <- if (n_auth > 2L || grepl("et al", c1$authors %||% "")) {
    paste(sub(" [A-Z-]+$", "", first), "et al.")
  } else {
    sub(" [A-Z-]+$", "", first)
  }
  txt <- trimws(paste(who, c1$year %||% ""))
  if (!is.null(c1$doi) && nzchar(c1$doi)) {
    sprintf("[%s](https://doi.org/%s)", txt, c1$doi)
  } else if (!is.null(c1$url) && nzchar(c1$url)) {
    sprintf("[%s](%s)", txt, c1$url)
  } else {
    txt
  }
}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# The same for a citation written as one string: the authors and year before
# the first "(year)", else the text before the first full stop, linked to the
# first DOI in the string.
short_ref_text <- function(txt) {
  m <- regmatches(txt, regexec("^([^()]+?) \\((\\d{4})\\)", txt))[[1L]]
  label <- if (length(m)) {
    who <- trimws(m[2L])
    if (grepl(",", who) && !grepl("et al", who)) {
      who <- paste(sub(",.*$", "", who), "et al.")
    }
    sub(" [A-Z-]+ et al\\.$", " et al.", paste(who, m[3L]))
  } else {
    sub("[.(].*$", "", txt)
  }
  label <- sub("^([^ ]+) [A-Z]{1,3}( et al\\.)? ", "\\1\\2 ", label)
  doi <- regmatches(txt, regexpr("10\\.[0-9]{4,}/[^ ),;]+", txt))
  if (length(doi)) sprintf("[%s](https://doi.org/%s)", trimws(label), doi)
  else trimws(label)
}
```

This page lists every backbone taxify matches names against and every published dataset it can attach, with the version, size, licence and reference of each. The tables are generated from the manifest of this taxify version when the site is built. Installation is covered in [Get started](../taxify.html); how to choose backbones is in [Choosing and combining backbones](../backbones.html), and how to attach datasets in [Attaching published data](../enrichments.html).

In R, the same lists are returned by these functions:

```{r calls, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
list_backbones()     # the backbones
list_enrichments()   # the published datasets
list_traits()        # the traits add_trait() gathers across datasets
taxify_databases()   # backbones and datasets in one table
```

## Backbones

A backbone is downloaded once, on first use, and read from disk after that. `Names` counts accepted names and synonyms together.

```{r backbones}
bb <- list_backbones(verbose = FALSE)
bb$ref <- vapply(bb$name, function(n) short_ref(manifest$backends[[n]]),
                 character(1))
bb$licence <- vapply(bb$name, function(n) {
  manifest$backends[[n]]$license %||% ""
}, character(1))
bb$name <- sprintf("`%s`", bb$name)
knitr::kable(
  bb[, c("name", "title", "scope", "n_names", "size_mb", "version",
         "licence", "ref")],
  col.names = c("Backbone", "Full name", "Scope", "Names", "MB", "Version",
                "Licence", "Reference"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "l", "l", "l"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

The licence of a backbone without one in the table is set by its source; the `source` link of `list_backbones()` leads to it. AlgaeBase, FishBase and SeaLifeBase are licensed for non-commercial use only.

## Published datasets

Each dataset is attached by its `add_<source>()` function, whose help page lists its columns and reference. `Rows` counts the rows of the built dataset, which holds a row under every accepted name any backbone gives a species, so it is larger than the number of species in the source. A dataset marked `fixed` is a single release that is never updated; the others are updated when their source publishes a new version.

```{r datasets}
en <- list_enrichments(verbose = FALSE)
en <- en[order(en$name), ]
exports <- getNamespaceExports("taxify")
fn <- paste0("add_", en$name)
en$fun <- ifelse(fn %in% exports,
                 sprintf("[`%s()`](../reference/%s.html)", fn, fn), "")
en$licence <- vapply(en$name, function(n) {
  manifest$enrichments[[n]]$license %||% ""
}, character(1))
en$ref <- vapply(en$name, function(n) short_ref(manifest$enrichments[[n]]),
                 character(1))
en$release <- ifelse(en$static, "fixed", "updated")
knitr::kable(
  en[, c("name", "fun", "version", "release", "nrow", "licence", "ref")],
  col.names = c("Dataset", "Function", "Version", "Release", "Rows",
                "Licence", "Reference"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "l", "l"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

A dataset without a function of its own is attached through `add_trait()`, which reads it as one source of a trait.

## Traits across datasets

`add_trait()` gathers one trait from every dataset in the `From` column, in one unit and one vocabulary.

```{r traits}
tr <- list_traits()
tr <- tr[order(tr$trait), ]
tr$trait <- sprintf("`%s`", tr$trait)
knitr::kable(
  tr[, c("trait", "label", "kind", "unit", "n_sources", "sources")],
  col.names = c("Trait", "Label", "Kind", "Unit", "Sources", "From"),
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "l"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
